title: Nvidia in crisis amid probe into CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: CBS News correspondent Bradley Blackburn reports on the turmoil at Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects of spying for China, which has triggered a board inquiry, a shareholder lawsuit and questions from lawmakers. Nvidia's shares have lost hundreds of billions of dollars in value as investors ask whether Huang can stay, while the company insists no secrets were compromised and Beijing rejects the spying claims. Financial journalist Bill Cohan then weighs in on the fallout, including how dependent Nvidia is on a single leader and how the board's lack of an obvious successor complicates any decision.
focus: Shadow Blackburn's opening report that lays out the allegations and the market reaction, then the stretch where Cohan explains what the board's options are and why replacing Huang would be so difficult.
